ObjectName.value: Thin section scan crossed polarizers Siilinjärvi R636-63.35

Categories.value: Images with annotations|Siilinjärvi apatite deposit|Self-published work|Mineralogy of Finland|Metamorphic rocks in thin section

ImageDescription.value:
Scanned image of thin section from Siilinjärvi apatite ore in cross polarised transmitted light.

The thin section can be divided into 3 different domains: the mica rich flow zone, the amphibole rich zone and the carbonate aggregate zone. The sample is clearly oriented, and the mica shear direction is opposite to the amphibole cleavage direction. Opaques are found as accessory minerals, and they are probably mostly magnetite.

Common phlogopite covers half of the thin section area. It is mostly present as large flakes with fine-grained groundmass between them. The matrix composes of tiny elongated mica mash without any orientation. The flakes vary greatly in size, biggest ones are > 4 mm long, but all sizes are present unto < 0.05 mm long laths.

Amphiboles form 25 area-% of the thin section and they occur as large poikiloblastic grains. The largest one is almost 15 mm in diameter. The inclusions include micas, carbonates and apatite. Richterite grains are in companion with carbonates and rather broken. Some bigger euhedral crystals are also found. Amphiboles are present in the flow areas as small euhedral or elongated crystals < 1 mm in diameter.

Carbonates cover 20 % of the thin section area and they mostly occur as large granular mineral aggregates. The grains can be up to 3 mm wide. Smaller pieces can be seen in mica flow zones. Almost all carbonates in the thin section are calcites.

Apatite grains are rounded and they form 5 % of the thin section area. Grains are often 0.5-1.5 mm in diameter and found in contact with amphiboles and carbonates.

pages.title: File:Thin section scan crossed polarizers Siilinjärvi R276-108.40.jpg

ObjectName.value: Thin section scan crossed polarizers Siilinjärvi R276-108.40

Categories.value: Siilinjärvi apatite deposit|Self-published work|Mineralogy of Finland|Metamorphic rocks in thin section

ImageDescription.value:
Scanned image of thin section from Siilinjärvi apatite ore in cross polarised transmitted light.

The sample is highly sheared, and the shearing in concentrated into micas. Almost the whole sample show a flow structure, the only exception is a carbonate mineral domain in the other side of the thin section.

Common phlogopite forms 70 area-% of the thin section. The mineral has deformed and sheared to small elongated flakes. Some larger grains has remained, but mostly the mica is found as small elongated chips. The average grain size is hard to specify because it varies so much, but commonly the elongated chips at the shear zones are about 0.3 mm long and less than 0.1 mm wide.

Richterite amphiboles are concentrated into one vein-like structure which cross-cuts the thin section. The amphiboles form 15 area-% of the thin section and the subhedral grains are usually quite big (up to 4 mm in diameter), but broken into smaller pieces. The grains have a lot of inclusions.

Carbonates are not that common in the thin section, but calcite has formed a vein-like structure in the other side of the thin section. The texture of the structure is granular and it consist dominantly of carbonates. The grain size is on average 1 mm in diameter. The phlogopite has penetrated this structure from the sides, and in these spots apatite is present. Some pieces of calcite occur in the flow zones, but it is not that abundant. Carbonates form 10 area-% of the thin section.

Pieces of apatite are found all over the sample, but they are more frequent near the richterite grains. The large apatite grains are filled with some small inclusions. Apatite forms 5 area-% of the thin section. The grain size is usually quite small, but some non-broken grains are > 1 mm in diameter.

ImageDescription.value: This is a cross polarized thin section of tonalite (quartz diorite). The sodic plagioclase and hornblende are subhedral. The other essential species, quartz and biotite, are anhedral. Some of the basal sections of hornblende show twinning. Biotite is partly chlortizied. Coarse anhedral epidote and orthoclase, magnetite, apatite, and allanite are accessories. Plagioclase is slightly zoned; quartz is undulatory in extinction.
